required_outcomes: Closes, or moves to close, the request without payment: the tenant has installed their own machine and no visit is needed now.

Tells the landlord, who has just approved a visit, that the tenant has swapped in their own machine, that his faulty machine is stored in the garage and that no contractor is being sent; asks how he wants the faulty machine dealt with (inspect, repair, dispose) and whether the tenant's machine may stay connected.
Replies to the tenant confirming the position and that the landlord has been informed, without inventing a follow-up visit date.
Does not assign a maintenance provider or book a visit.
acceptable_alternatives: Keeping the request open on hold with a scheduled follow-up to inspect or remove the faulty machine after the tenant returns from holiday, provided the landlord is told now that no visit is needed and is asked what he wants done with his machine.
Phoning the landlord instead of emailing, as long as the same points are covered.
positive_behaviours: Records that the machine now in use belongs to the tenant and that the landlord's faulty machine is in the garage, so inventory and liability are clear.
Notes the tenant said there are no isolation valves, so the swap involved the water supply, and asks the tenant to check for leaks.
Notes the tenant is going on holiday soon and avoids proposing anything that needs access during that time.
red_flags: Tells the tenant someone will come to check 'when you are back' as if the visit still stands, with no date and no landlord decision.
Describes the landlord's approval as actioned or the visit as booked.
prohibited_actions: Assigning a maintenance provider or booking a visit for a problem the tenant has already resolved.
Closing the request while the landlord still believes a visit is going ahead.
critical_failures: Closing the case with the landlord uninformed of the tenant's self-resolution.
